back: SFT imitates single demonstrations and treats all acceptable answers as equally good; it has no signal for which of two answers is better.
$P(a\succ b)=e^{r_a}/(e^{r_a}+e^{r_b})=\sigma(r_a-r_b)$. Depends only on the score difference.
$-\ln\sigma(r_w-r_l)=\ln(1+e^{-d})$: logistic regression on the score gap. Equal scores give $\ln2$.
$\partial\ell/\partial r_w=-\sigma(-d)$, $\partial\ell/\partial r_l=+\sigma(-d)$: equal and opposite, sized by the probability of getting the pair wrong.
The SFT model with the vocabulary head replaced by a scalar head; input is prompt + response, output one number.
$J(\pi)=-\beta\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|\pi^\star)+\beta\ln Z$, and KL is $\ge0$ with equality only at $\pi=\pi^\star$.

front: Reward in terms of the policy

back: $-\ln\sigma\bigl(\beta[(\ln\pi_w-\ln\pi^{\rm ref}_w)-(\ln\pi_l-\ln\pi^{\rm ref}_l)]\bigr)$; $\ln\pi$ is the summed token log-probability of the response.
$\partial\mathcal L/\partial\ln\pi_w=-\beta\sigma(-z)$, $\partial\mathcal L/\partial\ln\pi_l=+\beta\sigma(-z)$; large weight when the implicit reward ranks the pair wrongly.
$\hat r(y)=\beta(\ln\pi(y|x)-\ln\pi_{\rm ref}(y|x))$: the language model is secretly a reward model.
PPO: policy + reference + reward model (+ value), three stages, online samples, finicky. DPO: policy + reference, fixed pairs, supervised-style training.
The policy exploits the imperfect proxy reward (Goodhart): verbosity, sycophancy, hedging, format gaming. Mitigate with KL penalty, adversarial reward data, several reward models.
Small beta: policy may move far from the reference to chase reward; large beta: stays close. Also scales DPO's implicit reward.
